quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, what is the best thing to do?

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.
Change your path as needed.
Use the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your path as needed.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and motorcycles with sidecars turn differently than two-wheeled motorcycles. The best path through a curve may not follow the curve itself. You may need to move from the outside of the curve to the inside before straightening out.

questions.question: When is it important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When approaching a police officer.
When someone is following too closely.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When someone is following too closely.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down if someone is following too closely. The other driver may not notice the hazard ahead that is making you slow. Also flash your brake light if you are about to slow down in a place where other drivers might not expect it.

questions.question: When picking a helmet, make sure it has all of the following, except:

options.text: U.S. Department of Transportation safety approval.
A snug fit.
No damage or defects.
An attractive look.

questions.correctAnswerText: An attractive look.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state safety standards. It should fit snugly all the way around. Check that it has no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: How should you pack a load on a motorcycle?

options.text: Put heavier items toward the front.
Put heavier items toward the rear.
Mount loads behind the rear axle.
Store lighter items in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items toward the front.
questions.explanation: Place heavier items toward the front of the load. Keep loads over or in front of the rear axle. Pack lighter items behind you.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use the front brake hard to prevent the front tire from locking.
Use only the rear brake.
Use either the front or rear brake, but not both.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down. Squeeze the brake lever slowly to avoid locking the front wheel. Use gentle pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Increase your ability to see.
Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Give you an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and surface hazards. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed.
Body weight.
How quickly the alcohol was consumed.
How often alcohol is consumed.

questions.correctAnswerText: How often alcohol is consumed.
questions.explanation: Three major factors affect BAC: how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. A person's sex, physical condition, and whether they have eaten may also have some effect.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power does the front brake supply?

options.text: About 25 percent.
About 50 percent.
About 70 percent.
100 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of a motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Where should a child passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: In front of the operator.
Behind the operator.
They do not need to reach the footrests.
They should hold onto the motorcycle frame.

questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the operator.
questions.explanation: A child passenger should always sit directly behind the operator. A child in front may not balance properly and could get in the way of the operator's controls.

questions.question: When an operator's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, what does it mean?

options.text: The operator plans to turn left.
The operator is about to stop.
The operator plans to turn right.
The operator is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The operator plans to turn right.
questions.explanation: Operators use hand signals instead of mechanical turn signals to show turns or stops. When the left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, it means the operator plans to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: When riding in a group, you should:

options.text: Never use a staggered formation.
Place inexperienced riders at the back of the group.
Not use your mirrors.
Keep proper space between you and other riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep proper space between you and other riders.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, use a staggered formation. Check your mirrors often to see riders behind you. The lead and sweep riders should be experienced. Always keep enough space between riders.

questions.question: Swerving a motorcycle:

options.text: Requires a lot of traction.
Requires little traction.
Is a slow maneuver.
Should be done to avoid a hazard on a slippery road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Requires a lot of traction.
questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick maneuver that needs lots of traction to do safely. Do not swerve on wet or slippery surfaces.

questions.question: It is most important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: Switching into a neutral gear.
You will slow down suddenly.
There is a stop sign ahead.
Your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before you slow down suddenly. This warns a tailgater who may not see hazards ahead that you are slowing down.

questions.question: Proper footwear for riding a motorcycle:

options.text: Has long, loose laces.
Has short heels.
Has tall heels.
Is always sneakers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has short heels.
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels can catch on things. Tuck in any loose laces.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle best, a rider should:

options.text: Sit with their arms fully extended.
Use their arms to hold their body up.
Keep their knees away from the gas tank.
Keep their feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep their feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Use your arms to control the motorcycle, not to hold yourself up. Keep your arms slightly bent. Press your knees against the gas tank and keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, you should:

options.text: Speed up before contact.
Slow down before contact.
Lean the motorcycle.
Stay seated on the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before contact.
questions.explanation: Slow down as much as you can before hitting the object. Keep the motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off the seat and ease off the throttle just before impact.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane give a motorcyclist?

options.text: One
Two
Three
Four

questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane provides three paths of travel for motorcyclists: the left, center, and right areas of the lane.

questions.question: A proper lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Allow you to set up for turns.
Allow an escape route.
Allow you to avoid wind blasts from other vehicles.
Place you in another vehicle's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place you in another vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, maintain a minimum following distance of:

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Always maintain at least two seconds of distance behind the vehicle in front of you. Increase this distance if conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters. You must follow all rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: You must finish the pass in a passing zone.
You may finish the pass in a no-passing zone if you started before the zone began.
You should make eye contact with the other driver.
You should ride on the shoulder if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must finish the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: All passes must be completed in passing zones only. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, you may need to adjust all of the following, except:

options.text: Tire pressure.
Mirror positions.
Headlight position.
Brake light position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake light position.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle sits differently with a passenger because of the extra weight. You may need to adjust tire pressure, suspension, shocks, headlights, and mirrors. Brake light position does not need adjustment.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
Press the handle grip in the opposite direction of where you want to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve and avoid a hazard, press the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then press the right to recover. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: What is the best lane position?

options.text: Always ride on the right side of the lane.
Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride on the left side of the lane.
Change your position based on road, weather, and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your position based on road, weather, and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your lane position based on current riding conditions.

questions.question: If you need to brake while in a curve, you should:

options.text: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
Brake as hard as you would on a straight road.
Wait until you are out of the curve to brake.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans, the tires have less grip. Try to straighten up before braking. If you must brake in a curve, apply the brakes smoothly and gently.

questions.question: How can you regain control if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Release the rear brake.
Keep using the rear brake.
Swerve toward the safest area.
Try to accelerate while braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Release the brake to regain control of a locked rear wheel. However, if the rear brake locks on good pavement, you can keep it locked until the motorcycle stops.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, tell them to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine starts.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Talk whenever they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk whenever they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should not talk or move unnecessarily so you can focus on riding. Passengers should board after the engine starts, sit forward without crowding you, and hold your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Which is a poor reason to sound your horn?

options.text: A driver next to you is too close to the vehicle ahead.
A parked car has someone in the driver's seat.
You want people to notice your motorcycle.
You are passing a pedestrian on the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to notice your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sound your horn to warn vehicles or pedestrians who may move into your lane. It is good to horn before passing a vehicle, a parked car with someone inside, or a pedestrian. Do not use the horn just to get attention.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Use your high beam.
Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Be visible.
Ride only in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Use your high beam (unless following or meeting another vehicle), use other vehicles' headlights to help you see, and wear reflective materials. Change your lane position as needed to see better, be seen, and stay safe.

questions.question: If you brake while in a curve:

options.text: Use only the front brake.
It is the same as braking on a straight road.
You will have more traction as you lean.
You may have less traction as you lean.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less traction as you lean.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be careful. When the motorcycle leans, some tire grip is used for turning, leaving less grip available for stopping.

questions.question: What color is a warning sign with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, you should:

options.text: Always ride in the center portion of the lane.
Always ride in the left portion of the lane.
Always ride in the right portion of the lane.
Change your position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Choose the position where you are most visible and can keep space around you.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Ride under the speed limit.
Keep your fingers on the clutch and brake levers.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Accelerate before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your fingers on the clutch and brake levers.
questions.explanation: When approaching dangerous areas like intersections, keep your fingers ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces your reaction time if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Checking your mirrors:

options.text: Is a bad idea because you should focus on the road ahead.
Is only important if you think there is a reason to check.
Helps you make safe riding decisions.
Should only be done when there is no other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps you make safe riding decisions.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly and look over your shoulder. You need to know what is on all sides of your motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding, you should NOT:

options.text: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
Point your toes down.
Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Use a headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
questions.explanation: Your arms should be used for steering, not for holding yourself up. Keep your knees on the gas tank and your toes pointed up. Always use your headlight.

questions.question: When using the front brake, you should:

options.text: Squeeze the lever smoothly with increasing pressure.
Grab the brake with only two fingers.
Press down on the brake lever with your foot.
Stomp on the brake lever.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever smoothly with increasing pressure.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the brake lever with all four fingers. Apply pressure smoothly and gradually for best braking control.

questions.question: How can you discourage other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Swerve from side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane to discourage cars from trying to share your space.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane.
Change your lane position as road and traffic conditions change.
Only ride in the center of the lane so other drivers can see you.
Ride in a zigzag pattern so other drivers notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position as road and traffic conditions change.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Move your position as needed based on changing road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: If your throttle gets stuck, you should:

options.text: Jump off the motorcycle.
Apply the brakes.
Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Not try to twist the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: Try twisting the throttle back and forth several times to free it. If that does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you properly if:

options.text: You can reach the footrests while seated.
Your feet can touch the ground while you are seated.
The seat comes up to your knees while you are standing.
You cannot reach the controls while seated.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your feet can touch the ground while you are seated.
questions.explanation: For a proper fit, your feet should reach the ground when you are seated. You should also be able to reach all controls easily.

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Can help protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Is not recommended because it can cause heat-related problems.
Should only be worn if the jacket is light colored.
Is not important.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants in hot weather. They protect you from crashes and also help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.

questions.question: When a vehicle is passing you from behind, you should:

options.text: Move to the shoulder.
Use the left part of your lane.
Use the center of your lane.
Use the right part of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: The center of your lane is the safest position when being passed. Riding close to the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding far from it may make the driver return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: Your riding clothes should protect you from all of the following, except:

options.text: Sunburn.
Windburn.
Chapped lips.
Dehydration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Chapped lips.
questions.explanation: Your riding clothes should protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, dehydration, cold, and motorcycle parts. Good clothing also protects you in a crash.

questions.question: When a vehicle is passing you from behind, you should:

options.text: Move to the center of your lane.
Move to the left of your lane.
Move to the right of your lane.
Not worry about where you are in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. This reduces the risk of hitting the passing vehicle.

questions.question: If a driver is following you too closely, you should:

options.text: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn the driver.
Speed up.
Pull over to the side of the road.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn the driver.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down if someone is tailgating you. The tailgater may not see road hazards ahead that require slowing.

questions.question: To avoid getting tired on a long ride, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Dress warmly.
Limit the distance you ride in a day.
Take frequent rest breaks.
Take artificial stimulants.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take artificial stimulants.
questions.explanation: Protect yourself from tiring weather conditions like wind and rain. Ride no more than 6 hours per day and take a break at least every 2 hours. Do not use artificial stimulants because extreme tiredness may happen when they wear off.

questions.question: When entering a highway or curve, motorcyclists in a group should:

options.text: Ride single-file.
Ride in a staggered formation.
Ride in pairs.
Ride on the far right of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride single-file.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation normally, but switch to single-file when turning, going around curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?

options.text: Once a day
Once a week
Once a year
Before every ride

questions.correctAnswerText: Once a week
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride for safety. Check hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the grip opposite the direction you want to turn.
Not hold the grip because it can be dangerous.
Not lean the motorcycle because it can be unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When riding faster than a walk, your motorcycle needs to lean to turn. Pressing the grip in the direction you want to turn makes the motorcycle lean the right way.

questions.question: When making normal stops, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both the front and rear brakes.
Alternate between the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping, even for normal stops. Make this a habit.
